reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Urea -> Produced in the liver as a waste product of protein metabolism -> Transported to the kidneys for excretion -> 80% CHAIN: Urea -> Not degraded to ammonium in the urea cycle -> 20% CHAIN: Urea -> Polar molecule due to the presence of the amino group -> Does not easily form crystals -> 70% CHAIN: Urea -> Derived from ammonia and carbon dioxide in the liver -> 90% CHAIN: Urea -> Contains one carbonyl group and one amino group, not two ketone groups -> 80%
enhanced_information: Urea is produced in the liver as a waste product of protein metabolism, then transported to the kidneys for excretion. It is not degraded to ammonium in the urea cycle. Urea is a polar molecule due to the presence of the amino group and is derived from ammonia and carbon dioxide in the liver. It contains one carbonyl group and one amino group, not two ketone groups. Relevant evidence supports urea's interaction with enzymes in the liver and its presence in liver cells.
analysis: Urea is a waste product of protein metabolism produced in the liver and excreted by the kidneys. It is not degraded to ammonium in the urea cycle but is derived from ammonia and carbon dioxide. Urea is a polar molecule due to the amino group and contains one carbonyl group and one amino group. The statement that urea is transported to the liver for elimination is incorrect. The correct information aligns with urea being produced in the liver and excreted by the kidneys.
